gaps.sentence: 'The train left ten minutes ago,' she said. She said the train ___ ten minutes before.
gaps.explanation: Past simple becomes past perfect, and 'ago' becomes 'before': had left ten minutes before.

gaps.sentence: 'I work from home on Fridays,' he explained. He explained that he ___ from home on Fridays.
gaps.explanation: After a past reporting verb, present simple backshifts to past simple: work → worked.

gaps.sentence: "Where do you live?" — He asked me where I ___.
'Who broke the window?' the teacher demanded. The teacher demanded ___ the window.
gaps.explanation: 'Demand to know + wh-clause' with statement order; past simple backshifts to past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll see you tomorrow,' he said. He said he would see me ___.
gaps.explanation: Time expressions shift: tomorrow becomes the next day / the following day.

gaps.sentence: 'No, I won't open the door,' he said. He ___ to open the door.
gaps.explanation: Refusals are reported with refuse + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'I moved here two years ago,' he explained. He explained that he had moved there two years ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Ago' becomes 'before' (or 'earlier') in reported speech; here → there as well.

gaps.sentence: 'Please don't smoke in here,' the host said. The host asked me ___ in there.
gaps.explanation: Negative requests: asked me not to smoke; 'here' shifts to 'there'.
